content:
meera: Quick sync — I sketched a proposal for a 'hybrid rollback adjudicator' that decides canary -> full rollout transitions and automatic fallbacks. TL;DR: combine probe metrics (latency, errors), real user impact signals, and cost delta into a single decision score. Looking for feedback on API boundaries and telemetry needs.

liam: Nice. Is this separate service or part of the runtime controller?

meera: Separate service (stateless adjudicator) that subscribes to aggregated telemetry snapshots. Runtime implements a small control API to accept adjudicator commands (continue/rollback/redirect). Keeps runtime surface minimal.

sam: Two quick concerns: 1) decision latency (we can't block traffic) and 2) testability — want deterministic sim mode.

meera: Agreed. Adjudicator should emit nonblocking recommendations and a confidence score. Runtime applies a safety policy: only act on decisions above confidence threshold OR after a manual override. Sim mode is mandatory for staging.

nora: Can you sketch config / decision contract? rough idea: 
```
adjudicator:
  window_seconds: 300
  min_requests: 500
  signals:
    - name: latency_p95
      weight: 0.4
      threshold_ms: 300
    - name: error_rate
      weight: 0.4
      threshold: 0.015
    - name: quality_regression
      weight: 0.2
      threshold: 0.02
  verdict_thresholds:
    rollback: 0.7
    continue: 0.3
```

meera: That's the idea. Adjudicator computes a weighted score and maps into verdict buckets: ROLLBACK, PAUSE, CONTINUE, ESCALATE.

liam: How do we get quality_regression in near real-time? eval runs are heavy.

meera: We lean on lightweight proxy metrics: prompt-level heuristics (e.g., repetition, toxicity flags), a small set of golden prompts sampled from traffic, and an offline eval signal fed with lower weight. The adjudicator tolerates delayed signals.

sam: What about interface? I suggest a single endpoint from runtime to adjudicator: POST /v1/rollouts/{id}/snapshot -> returns {verdict, confidence, reason_tags}. Runtime also exposes: POST /v1/rollouts/{id}/action to accept instructions.

nora: Example payloads: 
```json
POST /v1/rollouts/abc123/snapshot
{
  "traffic_summary": {"requests": 1200, "p95_ms": 310, "error_rate": 0.012},
  "quality_signals": {"golden_score": 0.985, "prompt_flags": 0.02},
  "cost_delta": 0.08
}

Response:
{ "verdict": "PAUSE", "confidence": 0.62, "reason_tags": ["latency_p95", "cost_delta"] }
```

meera: Nice and compact. Runtime can act on response or forward it to an operator UI.

infra-bot: [deploy-bot] canary/adjudicator v0.1 deployed to staging at 2026-03-15T14:10Z :rocket:

liam: Failure modes? We need a kill-switch if adjudicator becomes flaky. Also consider split-brain if multiple adjudicators disagree.

meera: Proposals:
- Runtime keeps a fallback to baseline variant and can immediately cut traffic there on adjudicator FAIL or on timeout.
- Adjudicators operate in leader-elected mode per rollout id (use Redis lease) to avoid conflicts.
- Add a circuit-breaker counter: if adjudicator issues more than N rollbacks in T minutes, auto-disable auto-rollback and notify ops.

sam: Observability checklist:
- raw snapshots (for debug) stored for 7d
- verdict events (immutable) + input snapshot hash
- diff view between baseline/canary metrics
- ability to replay a window in sim mode

nora: Ownership: platform owns adjudicator service + UI; runtime implements 3 small endpoints and a fallback path; product defines risk budgets for each customer/route.

meera: Operational questions: what SLA for adjudicator? I propose soft SLO: 99.9% availability, but we tolerate slower responses (adjudicator can be async). Need alerting on high undecided rate.

liam: Rollout plan idea: 1) Prototyping behind feature flag (no automatic rollbacks, only recommendations) 2) Canary on internal routes 3) Limited auto-rollback for low-risk routes 4) Gradual expansion with policy templates.

sam: Edge case: model variant mismatch (adjudicator sees metrics for variant v1 but rollout already moved to v2). Need strong snapshot tagging by variant hash.

meera: Yes: include model_hash and route_version in every snapshot, adjudicator must validate and reject stale snapshots.

infra-bot: [monitor] adjudicator-recommendation-latency > 1s (p95) in staging (observed at 2026-03-15T14:25Z) :warning:

nora: Action item: I'll draft a short RFC covering API schema, state machine, and telemetry retention. Can we sync Tuesday 10am?

meera: Tuesday 10am works. Thanks everyone — please add blockers in the RFC thread. :+1:
